Preschool.name: Getting Started & Task Engagement
items: Chooses an activity from a small set of available options.
Begins a familiar activity after a clear direction or cue.
Gets the materials needed for a familiar activity.
Moves from choosing an activity to starting it.
Joins a familiar group activity when it begins.
Starts a familiar arrival or departure routine.
Begins cleanup when the activity ends.
Approaches a new activity after a brief demonstration.
Resumes an activity after a short interruption.
Starts a familiar self-care step when it is time to do it.

Preschool.name: Attention & Persistence
items: Stays engaged in a chosen play activity long enough to develop the play.
Attends long enough to hear a short direction.
Participates in a brief group activity appropriate for their age.
Stays with a mildly difficult activity for a short period.
Returns to an activity after a distraction.
Completes a short activity with a clear endpoint.
Continues after making a small mistake.
Accepts help and continues with a difficult activity.
Notices when attention has moved away from the activity and returns.
Persists with an everyday task until the necessary steps are done.

Preschool.name: Routines & Sequencing
items: Follows the steps of a familiar daily routine in order.
Carries out two related directions in sequence.
Remembers what comes next in a well-practiced routine.
Uses a picture sequence or visual schedule to follow a routine.
Follows the sequence of a familiar game.
Imitates a short sequence of actions or movements.
Completes handwashing steps in a workable order.
Gets ready for snack or a meal in the expected sequence.
Follows a simple first–then direction.
Finishes one step before moving to the next step in an activity.

Preschool.name: Flexibility & Transitions
items: Stops one activity and begins the next after a transition cue.
Moves from a preferred activity to a necessary routine.
Adjusts when a familiar activity happens in a different order.
Accepts a small change to a play plan.
Tries another approach when the first one does not work.
Returns to an activity after an unexpected interruption.
Moves with the group between familiar locations.
Uses a transition warning to prepare for a change.
Continues participating when a preferred material is unavailable.
Recovers enough after a change to take part in what comes next.

Preschool.name: Play & Social Problem Solving
items: Suggests a play idea that another child can join.
Enters ongoing play using a workable approach.
Takes a turn during a familiar shared activity.
Follows simple rules of a familiar game.
Responds to another child's play idea.
Allows a peer a turn at leading or choosing.
Communicates a preference during shared play.
Uses words, gestures, or a practiced strategy to handle a simple play disagreement.
Seeks adult help when a peer problem cannot be resolved.
Returns to shared play after a brief disagreement.

Preschool.name: Communication & Help-Seeking
items: Communicates a need for help using an effective method.
Shows or tells another person what is not working.
Asks for clarification when unsure what to do.
Communicates a choice or preference clearly enough to act on it.
Shares information needed for another person to join an activity.
Responds to a relevant question during an activity.
Explains a simple idea in an order another person can follow.
Tells or shows an adult when a needed item is missing.
Communicates a need for a break or change of activity.
Gets an adult when a problem exceeds what they can manage.

Preschool.name: Organization of Things & Spaces
items: Finds a commonly used personal belonging.
Returns familiar toys or materials to their usual places.
Keeps materials together while completing an activity.
Sets up a workable space for play or a short task.
Gets the items needed before beginning a familiar activity.
Uses common materials in a way that supports completing the activity.
Notices when something needed for an activity is missing.
Clears or puts away materials when an activity is finished.
Keeps track of a coat, bag, bottle, or similar belonging during a routine.
Uses a simple storage or visual system to find or put away materials.

Preschool.name: Independence & Regulation
items: Participates in dressing steps appropriate to their opportunities and abilities.
Completes familiar toileting steps with the level of help currently appropriate.
Participates in handwashing or other everyday hygiene routines.
Manages familiar lunch or snack materials with available adaptations.
Waits briefly for a turn or desired item.
Stops an action after a clear safety cue.
Communicates or shows when they are becoming upset.
Accepts a familiar adult's help to settle after frustration.
Uses a practiced calming or coping action when upset.
Returns to an everyday activity after a manageable upset.

Adult.name: Work & Learning
items: Starts important work early enough to allow for completion.
Identifies which task needs attention first.
Breaks a large assignment or project into usable steps.
Tracks deadlines and upcoming responsibilities.
Returns to work after an interruption.
Completes routine tasks after the initial interest fades.
Brings needed information or materials to meetings, classes, or work sessions.
Records and follows through on actions agreed to in a meeting or conversation.
Maintains a workable view of ongoing projects.
Completes the final step needed to submit or deliver finished work.

Adult.name: Home & Daily Living
items: Maintains a workable laundry routine.
Finds commonly used belongings when needed.
Notices household tasks before they become urgent problems.
Completes cleaning often enough to keep the living space functional.
Replenishes food and household supplies before they run out.
Finishes a household task after starting it.
Returns items to places where they can be found later.
Handles recurring home responsibilities on a workable schedule.
Plans and carries out routine meals or food preparation.
Uses a routine or system to track household tasks.

Adult.name: Time & Transportation
items: Estimates how long familiar activities will take well enough to plan.
Starts getting ready early enough for a commitment.
Includes travel time when deciding when to leave.
Arrives at commitments at the intended time.
Notices when it is time to stop one activity and begin another.
Allows for predictable delays when planning.
Uses a calendar, timer, alarm, or equivalent aid effectively when needed.
Checks upcoming commitments early enough to prepare.
Notices when an activity is taking more time than intended.
Adjusts the plan when something takes longer than expected.

Adult.name: Money & Administration
items: Pays bills by their due dates.
Opens and responds to important notices.
Completes required forms before their deadlines.
Locates important personal or financial records when needed.
Reviews subscriptions and recurring charges.
Handles insurance or benefits tasks within required timeframes.
Prepares tax-related or other recurring paperwork in time.
Tracks financial commitments made to other people.
Reviews accounts often enough to notice an unexpected issue.
Completes the final submission or follow-up step of an administrative task.

Adult.name: Health & Self-Care
items: Follows an intended medication or treatment routine when applicable.
Schedules needed health appointments.
Attends scheduled health appointments.
Completes follow-up steps after an appointment.
Maintains eating routines that support daily functioning.
Maintains a sleep routine that supports everyday responsibilities.
Notices and responds to basic needs such as food, water, rest, or movement.
Reorders medication or health supplies before running out when applicable.
Makes room for personally important health routines.
Seeks care for a health concern within a reasonable timeframe.

Adult.name: Relationships & Family
items: Remembers commitments made to other people.
Follows through on shared responsibilities.
Responds to important messages within a workable timeframe.
Tracks plans made with family, friends, or other important people.
Listens long enough to understand another person's request or perspective.
Pauses before responding when emotionally activated.
Communicates when capacity is limited or help is needed.
Notices when someone is waiting for an action or answer.
Returns to repair a misunderstanding after conflict.
Coordinates responsibilities that depend on another person's schedule.

Adult.name: Digital Life & Information
items: Maintains a workable way to identify important email.
Finds a needed digital file or record.
Manages notifications so they do not repeatedly derail intended activity.
Captures actionable information that arrives through different channels.
Uses a calendar or equivalent system to track commitments.
Uses a task or reminder system consistently enough to be useful.
Recognizes when digital activity has pulled attention from the intended task.
Returns to the intended activity after checking a message or notification.
Completes an online form or digital task after opening it.
Distinguishes information that requires action from information that does not.

Adult.name: Personal Goals & Self-Management
items: Turns a personally important idea into a specific next action.
Begins a personal project without relying entirely on an imminent deadline.
Breaks a longer-term goal into manageable steps.
Returns to a project after time away from it.
Continues a worthwhile project after the initial excitement fades.
Tracks where a paused project was left.
Notices when a strategy or system has stopped working.
Adjusts a support or routine to fit the problem it is meant to solve.
Plans for situations in which stress, fatigue, or distraction predictably affects performance.
Reviews unfinished commitments often enough to decide what to do next.
